continuous vaccination and PVS are effective strategies to control disease, but the effect of vaccination is limited and it is necessary to take the time for the immune to obtain immunity and/or the possibility for them being infected before into account.

vaccination can decrease the disease prevalence, but the time for vaccinees to obtain the immunity and the possibility that they will be infected before this should be considered in the modeling process.
vaccination is helpful but there is a necessary time interval for the vaccinees (suspected individuals who have started vaccination) to obtain immunity.

the impact of vaccination strategies on disease dynamics.
the effect of vaccination on the spread of diseases.
the effect of vaccination on disease elimination.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the time for the vaccinated to obtain immunity is an important factor for disease elimination and should be considered in the mathematical models.
the vaccinee effect is important for the control of the disease and should not be neglected in the model.
vaccination is an effective way to control infectious diseases.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the time for the individuals to obtain immunity or to be infected before that should be taken into account in the study of vaccination strategies.
the time for the vaccinated individuals to obtain immunity and their possibility to be infected before that must be taken into consideration in vaccination strategies.
the effect of vaccination should be considered carefully and the time for the individuals to obtain immunity and their infectiveness during this period should be considered in the modeling process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the time interval between two doses should not be ignored in vaccination process.
the effect of vaccination should not be over evaluated.
we should not neglect the effect of the time for vaccinees to obtain full immunity or the possibility that they are infected before this when designing and evaluating a vaccination strategy.
